title: Objects for an MU
summary: Read-only unless marked. Network: interfaces (/sys/class/net), addresses (ip -j, else /proc), routes (/proc/net/route, ipv6_route), listening (/proc/net/tcp*, udp*), firewall (nft -a list ruleset as root: rules with handles, sets such as xtp_peers with elements, chains with hook and policy). Services: units, failed, enabled. MuAuditor: the estate MU audit (/opt/mu-tools, loaded at run time): findings, thin, error. Xtpd: installed, running, pids, socket, config, listens, logTail; bringUp(config) and bringDown are PROTECTED (not start/stop: ~start is the asynchronous send the check refuses). Mu gathers them: mu~net, mu~services, mu~audit, mu~xtpd, with hostname, kernel, uptime and boot id.
authority: built and tested (architecture Tom Dyer; coding and writing Claude (Opus 5.5), 2026-11-24)
invariants: Examining is open; starting is protected
A command line is read inside Xtpd but never exposed: it can carry secrets
procedure: Start with mu~audit and mu~net~listening; they find issues fastest

provenance.claim: Network, NetInterface, NetAddress, NetRoute, NetListen, Firewall
